column1: skm3-u4-ni-kurabete|Comparison with baseline year|去年に比べて、今年の冬はずっと雪が多い。|Compared to last year, this winter has far more snow.|Noun + に比べて evaluates the current situation against a prior baseline standard.

skm3-u4-ni-kurabete|Comparison of options|電車を利用するのは、車を運転するのに比べて、到着時間の予測が立てやすい。|Taking the train makes arrival times much more predictable compared to driving a car.|Verb-plain + のに比べて cleanly contrasts two nominalized action clauses.

skm3-u9-garu|Third-person observable desire|うちの猫は外に出たがって、ドアの前で鳴いている。|Our cat wants to go outside and is meowing in front of the door.|〜たがる describes an observable third-person desire through physical behavior.

skm3-u9-garu|Third-person negative sensation|彼は注射をひどく痛がっていた。|He was showing severe pain from the injection.|〜がる attaches to an adjective stem to report observed discomfort rather than claiming direct telepathy.

skm3-u10-ni-yoru-to|Citing statistical survey|最近の世論調査によると、内閣支持率はやや下落したそうだ。|According to a recent public opinion survey, cabinet approval ratings reportedly dropped slightly.|Noun + によると pairs with hearsay ending 〜そうだ to formally cite statistical data.

skm3-u10-ni-yoru-to|Citing rumor or eyewitness account|田中さんの話によれば、部長は来月転勤するらしい。|According to what Tanaka said, the department manager will apparently transfer next month.|Noun + によれば pairs with evidential conjecture 〜らしい.

skm3-fc-tokoro-datta|Narrow escape from missing train|もう少しで終電に乗り遅れるところだった。|I came within a hair's breadth of missing the last train.|もう少しで + V-る + ところだった describes an undesirable event narrowly averted at the last second.

skm3-fc-tokoro-datta|Narrow escape from accident|危うく赤信号を見落とすところだったが、手前で急ブレーキを踏んだ。|I almost overlooked the red light, but slammed on the brakes just before the intersection.|危うく + V-る + ところだった expresses relief at averting a collision.

skm3-fj-kimi|Slight touch of cold|朝から喉が痛くて、少し風邪気味です。|My throat has been hurting since morning, and I have a slight touch of a cold.|Noun + 気味 describes nascent physical symptoms before a full-blown illness.

skm3-fj-kimi|Nascent operational delay|悪天候のため、電車の運行が全体的に遅れ気味になっている。|Due to adverse weather, train operations are slightly lagging behind schedule overall.|Verb stem + 気味 indicates a slight unfavorable operational deviation.

genki1-wa-desu|Contextual topic omission|スミスさんは学生ですか。はい、（私は）学生です。|Are you a student, Smith-san? Yes, I am.|Once the topic is established by conversational context, Japanese naturally omits the pronoun.
genki1-wa-desu|Contrastive topic marking|昼ご飯は食べましたが、朝ご飯は食べませんでした。|I ate lunch, but as for breakfast, I didn't eat.|は marks contrast between two parallel contextual topics.

genki1-verb-groups|Ru-verb (Ichidan) drop-ru conjugation|食べる→食べます、見る→見ます、起きる→起きます。|Eat -> eat (polite); see -> see (polite); wake up -> wake up (polite).|Ru-verbs drop final る and attach ます without vowel alternation.

genki1-verb-groups|U-verb (Godan) vowel shift conjugation|書く→書きます、話す→話します、待つ→待ちます。|Write -> write (polite); speak -> speak (polite); wait -> wait (polite).|U-verbs shift the final u-vowel to the corresponding i-vowel before ます.
genki1-verb-groups|Irregular verbs|する→します、くる（来る）→きます（来ます）。|Do -> do (polite); come -> come (polite).|Irregular verbs する and くる conjugate with stem changes.
genki1-te-form|Sequence of actions|朝起きて、顔を洗って、朝ご飯を食べました。|I woke up in the morning, washed my face, and ate breakfast.|The te-form links successive actions in chronological order.
genki1-te-form|Polite request with ください|大事な話ですから、静かに聞いてください。|Because this is an important matter, please listen quietly.|V-て + ください forms a standard polite request.
genki1-te-iru|Action in continuous progress|今、部屋で日本語の文法を勉強しています。|Right now, I am studying Japanese grammar in my room.|Activity verbs in 〜ている express an action currently in active progress.
genki1-te-iru|Resulting continuous state|田中さんは窓の近くの席に座っています。|Tanaka-san is seated in the chair near the window.|Instantaneous change verbs (座る、結婚する、知る) in 〜ている express a lasting resultant state.
genki1-ndesu|Providing background explanation|どうして遅刻したのですか。電車が止まったんです。|Why were you late? It's because the train stopped.|〜んです provides an underlying causal explanation for an observed situation.
genki1-ndesu|Inviting clarification or detail|頭が痛いんです。少し休んでもいいですか。|The thing is, I have a headache. May I rest a little?|〜んです frames personal circumstances before requesting permission.

genki2-kanoukei|Potential verb with が particle flip|以前は泳げませんでしたが、今は一キロ泳げます。|Previously I could not swim, but now I can swim one kilometer.|Potential verbs commonly take が instead of を for the object of ability.
genki2-kanoukei|Circumstantial possibility|この図書館では、誰でも無料で本を借りることができます。|In this library, anyone can borrow books for free.|〜ことができる expresses circumstantial permission or institutional feasibility.

genki2-te-oku|Advance preparation for future use|明日友達が遊びに来るので、部屋を掃除しておきました。|Because my friends are coming over tomorrow, I cleaned my room in advance.|V-ておく denotes an action performed in preparation for a future event.
genki2-te-oku|Leaving a state as it is|窓を開けておいてください。部屋の空気を入れ替えたいので。|Please leave the window open, as I want to air out the room.|V-ておく can express leaving a resultant state intact for a purpose.
genki2-yasui-nikui|Ease of handling or doing|この辞書は文字が大きくて、とても使いやすい。|This dictionary has large print and is very easy to use.|Verb stem + やすい indicates that performing the action is facile or smooth.

genki2-yasui-nikui|Difficulty of handling or doing|字が小さすぎて、薄暗い部屋では読みにくい。|The font is too small, making it difficult to read in a dim room.|Verb stem + にくい indicates physical or cognitive difficulty in execution.

gp-nagara|Simultaneous actions by single agent|音楽を聞きながら、レポートを書いた。|I wrote the report while listening to music.|V-stem + ながら indicates two actions performed simultaneously by the same subject; the main action follows in clause two.
gp-nagara|Concessive contrast|悪いと知りながら、つい甘いものを食べてしまった。|Although knowing it was bad, I inadvertently ate sweets.|Concessive ながら admits a contradictory circumstance.

gp-saichuu|Interruption during meal|食事の最中に電話がかかってきて、話が中断した。|Right in the middle of our meal, the phone rang and our conversation was cut off.|〜最中に highlights an unexpected external disruption at the peak of an ongoing action.

gp-saichuu|Interruption during meeting|会議の最中に、突然停電が起きて真っ暗になった。|Right in the middle of the meeting, a sudden blackout occurred and everything went pitch dark.|External disruption occurring during an event.
gp-totan|Instantaneous sensory surprise|窓を開けたとたんに、冷たい風が吹き込んできた。|The very instant I opened the window, freezing wind swept in.|V-た + とたんに pairs with an unexpected, instantaneous physical reaction.
gp-totan|Instantaneous action|立ち上がったとたんに、めまいがして倒れそうになった。|The instant I stood up, I felt dizzy and almost collapsed.|Bodily reflex occurring immediately upon standing.

gp-kara-node|Subjective personal conviction with から|危ないから、絶対に触らないでください。|Because it is dangerous, please under no circumstances touch it!|から accommodates strong personal commands, warnings, and speaker volition.

gp-kara-node|Objective polite cause with ので|明日は私用がございますので、お休みをいただきます。|Because I have personal business tomorrow, I will take the day off.|ので smoothly and politely presents an objective causal ground in formal interaction.

gp-te-shimau|Unintended accident with regret|大切な書類を電車の網棚に忘れてしまった。|I inadvertently left my important documents behind on the train's luggage rack.|V-てしまう expresses deep regret over an irreversible mistake.
gp-te-shimau|Complete thorough execution|今日中にこの本を全部読んでしまおう。|Let us read this entire book completely through by the end of today.|V-てしまう denotes carrying an action through to its absolute finish.

gp-bakarini|Fatal trivial cause leading to disaster|嘘をついたばかりに、親友の信頼を完全に失ってしまった。|Simply because I told a lie, I completely lost my best friend's trust.|〜ばかりに indicates that one unfortunate action became the sole cause of a disastrous outcome.

gp-bakarini|Unqualified desire leading to regret|車を安く買いたいと思ったばかりに、故障ばかりの欠陥車を掴まされた。|Simply because I wanted to buy a car cheaply, I got saddled with a lemon that keeps breaking down.|A naive wish resulting in an ongoing nightmare.

gp-monodakara|Personal excuse for delay|事故で電車が止まってしまったものですから、遅刻してしまいました。|Because the train stopped due to an accident, I ended up late.|〜ものだから offers an excusing circumstance, conveying that circumstances beyond one's control were to blame.
gp-monodakara|Apologizing for oversight|急いでいたものだから、確認するのを忘れてしまいました。|Because I was in such a rush, I forgot to check.|Giving an understandable personal excuse in polite conversation.

gp-karaniwa|Resolute commitment to duty|引き受けたからには、最後まで責任を持ってやり遂げます。|Now that I have taken it on, I will see it through with responsibility until the end.|〜からには asserts that having crossed a threshold, one is honor-bound to follow through.

gp-karaniwa|High standard once participating|試合に出る以上は、全力を尽くして勝利を目指したい。|Since we are competing in the match, I want to give it our all and aim for victory.|〜以上(は) introduces a natural moral duty following from an established premise.

gp-sae-ba|Single essential requirement|パスポートさえあれば、とりあえず海外へ出国できる。|As long as you have your passport, you can at least depart for abroad.|Noun + さえ + Verb-ば identifies the single indispensable condition that makes everything possible.
gp-sae-ba|Minimal effort sufficient|薬を飲みさえすれば、すぐに熱は下がります。|As long as you just take the medicine, your fever will go down promptly.|Verb stem + さえすれば focuses on the single action required.

gp-toshitara|Pure counterfactual hypothesis|もし生まれ変わることができるとしたら、鳥になって空を飛びたい。|Supposing that I could be reborn, I would want to become a bird and fly in the sky.|〜としたら assumes a purely hypothetical, imaginative condition.

gp-toshitara|Logical conditional deduction|彼の証言が事実だとすれば、事件の全貌は一変する。|If his testimony is assumed to be true, the entire picture of the case completely changes.|〜とすれば deduces logical implications assuming a premise holds.
gp-dake-shika|Neutral limit with だけ|必要な分だけ取ってください。|Please take only the amount that you need.|だけ sets an objective boundary without implying insufficiency.
gp-dake-shika|Negative exclusion with しか〜ない|財布の中に百円しか残っていなかった。|There was only 100 yen left in my wallet.|しか…ない conveys that the remaining amount is lamentably small.

gp-wo-hajime|Singling out prime representative|総理大臣をはじめ、各国の首脳がサミットに集まった。|Starting with the prime minister, heads of state from various nations gathered at the summit.|〜をはじめ(として) introduces the most prominent representative member of a group.
gp-wo-hajime|City representing region|東京をはじめとする大都市では、交通網が高度に発達している。|In major metropolises, starting with Tokyo, transportation networks are highly developed.|Modifying a noun with 〜をはじめとする + Noun.

gp-ni-watatte|Extensive temporal duration|十年にわたる研究の末、ついに新薬の開発に成功した。|After research spanning a full decade, we finally succeeded in developing the new drug.|Modifying a noun with 〜にわたる + Noun over a ten-year duration.
gp-ni-watatte|Extensive geographical expanse|台風による被害は、県内全域にわたって広がっている。|Damage caused by the typhoon extends across the entire prefecture.|Describing wide geographical expanse.

gp-wo-tsuujite|Continuous span throughout an entire year|この地方は、年間を通じて温暖で過ごしやすい気候だ。|This region has a mild and pleasant climate throughout the entire year.|〜を通じて marks an unbroken temporal span from start to finish.

gp-wo-tsuujite|Indirect medium or intermediary|友人の紹介を通じて、現在の職場と巡り合うことができた。|Through an introduction by a friend, I was able to encounter my current workplace.|〜を通して / 〜を通じて indicates the intermediary channel of connection.

gp-noni-temo|Frustration at clash with expectation with のに|約束したのに、彼は時間通りに来なかった。|Even though he promised, he didn't come on time.|のに conveys speaker's disappointment and frustration that reality clashed with a reasonable expectation.

gp-noni-temo|Pure factual concession with ても|雨が降っても、明日の試合は予定通り行われます。|Even if it rains, tomorrow's match will be held as scheduled.|ても neutrally establishes a condition under which the main clause remains unaffected.

gp-warini-nishiteha|Subjective proportionality with わりに|このレストランは、値段のわりには料理の質がとても高い。|Considering the price, the quality of this restaurant's food is remarkably high.|〜わりに(は) evaluates whether output matches the input standard.

gp-warini-nishiteha|Defying a strict category standard with にしては|彼は日本に十年間住んでいるにしては、日本語があまり上手ではない。|For someone who has lived in Japan for ten years, his Japanese is not very good.|〜にしては judges against a rigid categorical expectation that should have produced a different result.

gp-hanmen-ippou|Contradictory reverse face with 反面|都会での生活は便利な反面、自然と触れ合う機会が少ない。|While life in the city is convenient, on the flip side there are few opportunities to touch nature.|〜反面 focuses on the inherent contradictory drawback of a positive state.

gp-hanmen-ippou|Parallel coexisting trend with 一方で|輸出が増加する一方で、国内の個人消費は伸び悩んでいる。|While exports are increasing, on the other hand domestic consumer spending is sluggish.|〜一方で juxtaposes two parallel macroeconomic trends.

gp-hazuda-kamoshirenai|High logical expectation with はずだ|彼は毎日熱心に勉強していたから、試験に合格するはずだ。|Because he studied diligently every day, he ought to pass the exam.|〜はずだ indicates strong deductive confidence grounded on evidence.

gp-hazuda-kamoshirenai|Uncertain possibility with かもしれない|午後は天気が崩れて、夕方から雪になるかもしれない。|The weather might deteriorate in the afternoon and turn to snow from evening.|〜かもしれない leaves open a genuine possibility without committing to certainty.

gp-ni-chigainai|Deductive conviction from evidence|あの自信に満ちた表情を見れば、プレゼンが成功したに違いない。|Looking at that expression full of confidence, the presentation must have succeeded.|〜に違いない expresses unwavering conviction deduced from observable evidence.

gp-ni-chigainai|Conviction based on character|真面目な彼のことだから、約束を忘れるはずがない。絶対に覚えているに違いない。|Knowing how diligent he is, there is no way he would forget; he must definitely remember.|Conviction based on familiar character traits.
gp-giving-receiving|Giving favor to someone with てあげる|道に迷っていた観光客に、駅までの道を教えてあげた。|I gave directions to the station to a tourist who was lost.|〜てあげる indicates doing a kind deed outward for someone else.

gp-giving-receiving|Receiving gracious favor with てもらう|パソコンの調子が悪かったので、詳しい友人に直してもらった。|Because my computer wasn't working properly, I had a knowledgeable friend fix it for me.|〜てもらう indicates humbly receiving an action done on one's behalf.
gp-voice-ladder|Passive voice with affected subject|先生に褒められて、とても嬉しかった。|I was praised by the teacher, and was very happy.|Passive 受身 elevates the recipient of an action to subject.

gp-voice-ladder|Causative-passive forced action|子供の頃、親に嫌いな野菜を無理やり食べさせられた。|When I was a child, I was forced by my parents to eat vegetables I disliked.|Causative-passive 使役受身 describes an action one was compelled to perform against one's wishes.

gp-keigo-core|Honorific respect elevating client action|お客様、こちらのお席でお待ちいただけますでしょうか。|Esteemed customer, could you kindly wait in this seat?|尊敬語 elevates the actions and choices of customers and superiors.

gp-keigo-core|Humble deference lowering speaker action|弊社の担当者より、折り返しお電話申し上げます。|Our company's representative will humbly telephone you back.|謙譲語 lowers the speaker's in-group actions to show deference to the counterpart.

gp-tamaranai-naranai|Unbearable physical urge with たまらない|昨夜は一睡もできなかったので、今眠くてたまらない。|Because I couldn't sleep a wink last night, I am dying of sleepiness right now.|〜てたまらない expresses overwhelming physical sensation that cannot be held back.

gp-tamaranai-naranai|Spontaneous deep emotion with ならない|遠く離れて暮らす両親の健康が、心配でならない。|The health of my parents living far away weighs on my mind so much that I cannot help worrying.|〜てならない describes spontaneous psychological emotions welling up from within.

gp-ippouda|Single-directional trend towards deterioration|少子高齢化が進み、地方の人口は減少する一方だ。|With the declining birthrate and aging population, rural populations keep on declining in one direction.|〜一方だ indicates an ongoing, accelerating change in a single direction.
gp-ippouda|Trend towards worsening inflation|景気の悪化に伴い、物価は上昇するばかりだ。|Accompanying economic stagnation, prices just keep on rising.|〜ばかりだ conveys that an adverse trend continues relentlessly.

gp-motoni-motozuite|Creative raw material with をもとに|この映画は、実在の人物の日記をもとに制作された。|This movie was produced based on the diary of a real person as creative raw material.|〜をもとに indicates creative raw material or inspirational basis.

gp-motoni-motozuite|Statutory and legal foundation with に基づいて|労働基準法に基づいて、従業員の労働時間を適正に管理する。|In accordance with the Labor Standards Act, we appropriately manage employee working hours.|〜に基づいて indicates a strict legal, statutory, or empirical foundation.

gp-ni-taishite|Target of action or attitude with に対して|目上の人に対しては、敬語を使って話さなければならない。|Toward superiors, one must speak using polite honorific language.|〜に対して marks the human or institutional target of an attitude or speech.

gp-ni-taishite|Subjective viewpoint evaluation with にとって|私にとって、日本語の習得は人生最大の挑戦である。|For me, mastering Japanese is the greatest challenge of my life.|〜にとって evaluates significance strictly from the perspective of the named subject.
